validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/ROUTE — well corroborated, independent of GEM/wiki. gem.wiki's own infobox already discloses that this row is a cross-border line: 'Length: 184.8 km (Moldova), 333 km' with the Moldova figure cited to Moldovatransgaz. I fetched Moldovatransgaz's live page directly (the sheet's cited domain moldovatransgaz.md now 301-redirects to a broken location header on their end -> use the successor domain mtg.md, verified live: https://mtg.md/ru/news/54). It names this exact route as one of MTG's 8 serviced trunk lines: 'Ананьев - черновцы - богородчаны (АЧБ)' [Ananyev-Chernovtsy-Bogorodchany] -- built to supply Moldovan consumers, 184.8 km within Moldova, diameter 1020 mm, capacity 9.1 bcm/y. Diameter and capacity match GEM's row EXACTLY (1020 mm; 9.10 bcm/y). This is a specific, independent, non-GEM-derived source that actually names this pipeline (not a generic aggregate citation), so the existence flag from the standing rules does not apply here. Corroborating (not cited, but read for context): GulfPub's PE World Map traces two named legs on exactly this corridor -- 'Annayev [Ananyev] - Sholdaneshti' (Ukraine->Moldova, 94.2 km geodesic) and 'Sholdaneshti - Khotin' (Moldova->Ukraine, Khotin being in Chernivtsi Oblast = the 'Chernovtsy' waypoint in MTG's full name) -- both flagged diameter-match against P1481 and both scored P1481 as nearest GEM row (recon_gulfpub batch, near_misses/overlaps, batches/ukraine-gas/staging/recon-gulfpub-20260812/match_diff.json). Their capacity field is a flat placeholder (1700 MMcf/d, capacity_raw='Not specified' on every nearby segment) so it does not corroborate or contradict GEM's 9.1 bcm/y either way. Separately, OSM traces overlap 85-97% with P1481's already-drawn route geometry in three places (recon-osm-20260812/match_diff.json, all disposition=FRAGMENT_OF_EXISTING) -- real-world mapped infrastructure sits on the line GEM already drew. Together: an official operator's self-description naming the line with matching diameter+capacity, a second independent scraped dataset tracing the same corridor through the same border towns, and real OSM infrastructure under the drawn route. CAVEAT: the 333 km total is gem.wiki's own aggregate (184.8 km Moldova-portion + an unstated Ukraine-side balance of roughly 148 km); no source I found itemizes the full 333 km directly, so I did not restage it as a fresh REFS_ADDED fill -- it is internally consistent with the corroborated Moldova-portion figure and not contradicted by anything I found, so I am not flagging it as a spec discrepancy, just noting the total is not independently itemized end-to-end.

validity.recommendation: Verify/likely correct Owner2 from 'SNTGN Transgaz SA' to 'Moldovatransgaz' (or remove it if a second owner can't be substantiated) -- route to Update, not applied here.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Owner field currently reads 'Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine; SNTGN Transgaz SA'. SNTGN Transgaz SA is Romania's state gas TSO (Medias, Romania) -- a real company, but I can find no connection between it and this specific pipeline or its Moldovan-transit operator. gem.wiki's own infobox foots the Owner field to citations [2][3], which are TSOU's generic 'Key Facts' page and TSOU's LinkedIn company page (https://tsoua.com/en/about-us/key-facts/, verified via a 2025-04-21 Wayback capture since the live page 403s to non-browser requests: http://web.archive.org/web/20250421144750/https://tsoua.com/en/about-us/key-facts/) -- neither of which mentions Transgaz SA, Romania, or this pipeline at all. So 'SNTGN Transgaz SA' as co-owner has NO citation actually supporting it, contrary to how the footnote numbering presents it. Independent check: Moldovatransgaz's own history page (https://mtg.md/ru/about/history, fetched for context, not cited as a proposed ref) traces its lineage through Soviet-era Kishinev/Drokia gas-transport directorates into a company reorganized in 1999 under JSC 'Moldovagaz' -- and Wikipedia's Moldovagaz shareholder breakdown (Gazprom 50%+1, Moldovan government 35.33%, Transnistrian government 13.44%, others 1.23%) shows no Romanian Transgaz stake anywhere in that chain. The pipeline this row actually crosses is described by MTG itself as feeding Moldovan consumers (not the Balkan-transit corridor); MTG's OTHER lines that DO run toward the Balkans via Romania (e.g. the Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail and Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail lines, which correspond to GEM's P0786/P0784 family) are the ones where a Romanian counterpart would make more geographic sense -- my working hypothesis is that 'SNTGN Transgaz SA' was transposed onto this row from one of those, but I have not chased that down and am not asserting it as fact. Recommend Update re-verify or drop Owner2 rather than accept it as-is; the correct second owner, if any beyond TSOU, is far more likely to be Moldovatransgaz (which is already correctly named as co-Operator on this same row).

validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki's infobox tags StartYear1='1987' with the same citation [4] (Moldovatransgaz) used for diameter/capacity/Moldova-length. I fetched the exact cited page (https://mtg.md/ru/news/54, full text extracted) and confirmed by direct string search that '1987' does not appear anywhere on it -- the page lists route/diameter/capacity for all 8 MTG trunk lines but carries no construction/commissioning dates. Separately, MTG's company-history page (https://mtg.md/ru/about/history) does mention 1987 -- but for an unrelated fact: the 2 June 1987 creation of the Drokia Linear Production Directorate of the 'Prykarpattransgaz' production association (a compressor-station administrative reorganization at Drokia, on the Moldovan side of this general corridor), not the commissioning of this specific pipeline. It is plausible this line dates to the Soviet-era build-out of that period, but I found no source that actually states 1987 as THIS pipeline's start year, so per the 'source must agree with the specific value' rule I am not staging a ref for it. Not an existence-level concern (the line's Soviet-era Ukraine-Moldova corridor role is well established), but the current citation is unsupported and should be flagged/replaced rather than trusted.

validity.recommendation: Cluster-level adjudication needed vs P1485 (Kremenchuk-Anan'iv-Bohorodchany Gas Pipeline) -- do not merge without a human/geometry check.
validity.researcher_notes: P1485 'Kremenchuk-Anan'iv-Bohorodchany Gas Pipeline' shares TWO of P1481's three named waypoints (Anan'iv, Bohorodchany) and the same diameter (1020 mm), differing only in capacity (8.7 vs P1481's 9.1 bcm/y) and length (532 km vs 333 km) and in prepending a third far-off waypoint, Kremenchuk (Poltava Oblast, central Ukraine -- several hundred km from Anan'iv in the opposite direction from Bohorodchany). Two ways this resolves: (a) genuinely different physical pipes that happen to share an Anan'iv-Bohorodchany leg name and diameter by coincidence of the regional grid, or (b) P1485 is a mislabeled/duplicated entry that folds in this line's Anan'iv-Bohorodchany leg under an inflated route description. The independent evidence I found for P1481 (Moldovatransgaz naming exactly 'Ananyev-Chernovtsy-Bogorodchany' as ONE specific, complete, cross-border trunk with capacity 9.1 bcm/y) argues P1481 is the more soundly documented of the two and stands on its own -- but I have not found equivalent independent documentation for P1485's Kremenchuk waypoint or its 532 km/8.7 bcm/y figures, so I can't rule out overlap. Flagging per the standing duplicate-hunting instruction; not resolving myself.
